newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Seven buys ABC's Asia satellite TV unit.
newsitem.headline: Seven buys ABC's Asia satellite TV unit.

text.p: Television broadcaster the Seven Network Ltd announced on Thursday it had bought the Australia Television Asian satellite television service from the state-owned Australian Broadcasting Corp for an undisclosed price.

"The acquisition of Australia Television will underpin Seven's plans for the development of a significant presence for the company in Asia - with plans for the introduction of additional satellite programming channels for the Asian market," Seven said.

Australia Television, formed by the ABC four years ago, currently provides a free-to-air English language satellite television service covering most of the Asia Pacific region, reaching from Beijing in China in the north to Western Samoa in the east and India in the west.

Seven said it had established Seven Network Asia, which was developing a strong presence in Asian markets, principally China where Seven Network Asia was developing commercial television specific programming.
The ABC would continue to supply news and current affairs programming and the use of the ABC's Australia Television broadcast facilities and staff.

"Seven will work closely with the ABC in the development of programming for Australia Television - with plans to further strengthen programming to include Seven's news and current affairs, sports and locally produced programmes," Seven said.
Seven Chairman and controlling shareholder Kerry Stokes said in a statement the acquisition made sound business sense.
"Australia Television will provide the platform for Seven's plans for development in the world's fastest growing economic region," Stokes said.
Seven Managing Director Gary Rice said the introduction of digital technology, coupled with extensive satellite delivery abilities, would allow Seven to broaden its Asian programming.

"Seven will work closely with the ABC in further strengthening Australia Television - building from the television service's existing programming - and will undertake major marketing programmes to enhance advertiser involvement in the satellite service," Rice said.
Australia Television transmits on the Palapa C2 satellite which beams signals across the Asia Pacific region.
Seven said ABC also had an extensive terrestrial distribution network throughout the region.

Australia Television had access to a further nine-year lease on Palapa C2 transponder space, "space which provides additional audio and video signal capacity and is currently at a premium following several recent failures to launch new satellites."
The satellite system also had digital capabilities, which would allow for the development of a number of channels designed for specific Asian markets, Seven said.
